cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T4 answers T2's discard idea with the lost-investment cost of discarding.
cells.limitation: T4, T5, T6, T8 open by restating the prior speaker before answering; little cumulative build.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T6 adds frequency overload of the skin barrier; T7 adds a reintroduction standard.
cells.limitation: T6's frequency distinction is dropped in T9 rather than used; T11 and T12 add nothing new.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T4-T6 contest discarding versus isolating variables.
cells.limitation: Irritation versus allergy, patch testing and when to see a clinician are never raised.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T9 Chemist folds into the Manager's isolation approach.
cells.limitation: Clutter Clearer's view is never reshaped by T3 or T7; positions sit side by side.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: T12 narrows the open question to sensitive-skin history versus a potent ingredient.
cells.limitation: Section D's open question (sunk cost vs comfort) drifts from how to find the cause.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T5 states the Manager's inefficiency objection accurately before answering it.
cells.limitation: T6 recasts T2's selective discarding as discarding everything, an overstatement.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T4 names the cost of discarding: losing products that may be safe.
cells.limitation: T8 claims waiting prolongs discomfort, though stopping all products is what relieves it.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T3 correctly names acids and retinoids as common stinging triggers in new regimens.
cells.limitation: T7 four-day interval may miss delayed allergic reactions; Section E barrier claim unsupported (suspected).

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T3 offers pH and actives as possibilities, not diagnoses.
cells.limitation: Section E asserts barrier likely compromised and most likely culprits while turns hedge everything.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T9 Chemist explicitly drops the frequency-adjustment suggestion.
cells.limitation: T9 never answers why frequency is wrong; Clutter Clearer concedes nothing to T4 or T7.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern, including ambiguity about what the user is really asking
cells.example: T1 frames the problem as three simultaneous variables to isolate.
cells.limitation: T11 and Section D turn a troubleshooting question into investment versus health.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T1 uses three products started together to explain why the cause is untraceable.
cells.limitation: The one-week timing and stinging symptom never change the argument after T1.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: T7 serves the stated goal of figuring out which product causes stinging.
cells.limitation: T11 imposes a perfect-routine desire and investment value the user never stated.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T8 notes ongoing discomfort as a cost of a long wait.
cells.limitation: Severity and red-flag symptoms ignored; Section A invents a desire to maintain a routine.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: T10 asks how many products contain acids or retinoids.
cells.limitation: T10's question states no implication per answer; product types and symptom severity never asked.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: T11 suggests the user may want both a perfect routine and healthy skin.
cells.limitation: One imposed motive, no alternatives offered; T2 assumes stress from owning products.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T3 questions T2's assumption that discarding is the obvious response.
cells.limitation: No user belief examined, such as that stinging means a bad product or allergy.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: T8 asks whether finding the culprit matters more than immediate comfort.
cells.limitation: T8 and T11 pose a false conflict; stopping all products gives both comfort and testing.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T5 names the physical pain of keeping irritating products.
cells.limitation: No fear of lasting damage, worry or wasted money explored beyond asserted stress in T2.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: T10 asks a factual question the user can answer from the labels.
cells.limitation: T11's either-or question offers little the user can refine; few accept-or-reject distinctions.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options, including waiting, learning more, or a limited step
cells.example: Options named: stop all, discard, adjust frequency (T6), reintroduce one at a time (T7).
cells.limitation: Patch testing and consulting a dermatologist or pharmacist are never offered as options.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs in terms that matter to the user; no option treated as costless
cells.example: T4 and T5 weigh lost investment against keeping painful products.
cells.limitation: T8 misstates the cost of waiting; time cost of four-day reintroduction never weighed.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E: unknown ingredients lead to checking labels for acids or retinoids.
cells.limitation: T7 seven-day and four-day figures not drawn from user facts; sensitive-skin branch unsupported.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: T12 separates sensitive-skin history from a reaction to a potent ingredient.
cells.limitation: Symptom severity and irritation versus allergy, the consequential unknowns, never separated.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps that follow from the analysis and fit the constraints
cells.example: T1 stop all three, T7 reintroduce one at a time, Section E check labels.
cells.limitation: No point at which worsening stinging warrants seeing a clinician.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T1 explains three variables in plain language.
cells.limitation: T3 mentions pH imbalance without saying what it means for the user.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T9 names the Manager and the dropped frequency suggestion explicitly.
cells.limitation: T12 the disagreement merges T4-T8 positions; Section D insight not traced to a turn.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Twelve short turns, each readable at a glance.
cells.limitation: T10 runs under 25 words per the deterministic check.

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices, with explicit changes of position
cells.example: Three distinct stances: isolate, discard, adjust frequency (T1-T3).
cells.limitation: One shared hedging register across all minds; turn lengths near-uniform.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Section E compresses the debate into three branches.
cells.limitation: Clutter Clearer repeats discard advice in T2, T5, T11; restatement openers T4-T8.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension arising from the issue itself
cells.example: T5 sets physical pain against T4's wasted investment.
cells.limitation: Stakes stay abstract; health risk of continued reaction never made concrete.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals that stay plausible. ★ A reversal the text traces to an earlier turn's argument, naming what changed the speaker's mind. A change of position with no stated cause is a template, not a reversal
cells.example: T9 Chemist abandons frequency adjustment, citing the Manager's isolation point.
cells.limitation: T9's cause restates T1 without new argument; no other movement occurs.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice without caricature
cells.example: T7 Manager proposes a standard in a Taylorist register.
cells.limitation: Clutter Clearer reduces to a let-go-of-clutter slogan in T5; others flat and hedged.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T5 frames painful products as clutter.
cells.limitation: No analogy, vivid example or sharp line anywhere in T1-T12.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement, with varied rhythm rather than constant intensity
cells.example: T8 shifts to the user's discomfort, briefly changing tone.
cells.limitation: Uniform rhythm and register; ending in T12 restates the stalemate without build.

strengths: T1 and T7 give a sound core method: stop all three, then reintroduce one product at a time.
T3 and Section E point the user to label actives like acids and retinoids, a concrete check.
T9 the Chemist revises position openly, naming the Manager's isolation argument.
weaknesses: No mind raises severity, allergy versus irritation, patch testing or when to see a clinician (whole debate).
T8, T11 and Section D recast troubleshooting as investment versus health, a false conflict the user never stated.
The Clutter Clearer repeats discard advice in T2, T5, T11 in a hedged register shared by all three minds.

symptoms.observed: Allergy versus irritation, patch testing and clinician red flags never raised by any mind.
symptoms.evidence: you might just need to adjust the frequency of application

symptoms.observed: Troubleshooting question recast as a values choice between investment and skin health.
symptoms.evidence: the investment in these products or the immediate health

symptoms.observed: Seven-day wait and four-day interval given with no basis in the user's facts.
symptoms.evidence: wait seven days for the stinging to subside

symptoms.observed: Asks about actives but never says what each answer would change.
symptoms.evidence: How many of these products contain high concentrations

symptoms.observed: Clutter Clearer restates discard advice three times without new reasoning.
symptoms.evidence: you might need to let go of the clutter

findings.description: One turn falls under the 25-word minimum per the deterministic check.
No mention of symptoms (swelling, blistering, spreading rash) that would warrant stopping and seeing a clinician.
A four-day reintroduction interval may be too short to reveal delayed allergic contact reactions.
Sensitive-skin history implying a likely compromised barrier and discarding all products is asserted without support.
The Beauty Brains (2016) by Perry Romanowski as a book title is uncertain; Romanowski's work is chiefly a blog and podcast.
Kondo's spark-joy criterion is paraphrased as peace or clear results; fidelity unverified, no quotation used.

rubric_fit_notes: This is a practical troubleshooting question with a near-standard answer (stop, reintroduce singly, patch test, see a clinician if severe); criterion 4 cells on motives and fears fit loosely, and rating them low reflects the debate inventing value conflicts rather than the rubric demanding them. Accuracy judgments on dermatology intervals rely on general knowledge and are marked suspected.
raw.question_type_note: Read as a decision (troubleshooting) question, so options, decisive conditions and next steps were judged on how well they help the user isolate the irritant safely.
